Problem:

19.13 LAB*: Program: Pizza party weekend

Program Specifications. Write a program to calculate the cost of hosting three pizza parties on Friday, Saturday and Sunday. Read from input the number of people attending, the average number of slices per person and the cost of one pizza. Dollar values are output with two decimals. For example, print(f"Cost: ${cost:.2f}").

Note: this program is designed for incremental development. Complete each step and submit for grading before starting the next step. Only a portion of tests pass after each step but confirm progress.

Step 1 (2 pts). Read from input the number of people (int), average slices per person (float) and cost of one pizza (float). Calculate the number of whole pizzas needed (8 slices per pizza). There will likely be leftovers for breakfast. Hint: Use the ceil() function from the math library to round up to the nearest whole number and convert to an int. Calculate and output the cost for all pizzas. Submit for grading to confirm test 1 passes.
Ex: If the input is:

10  2.6  10.50

The output is:

Friday Night Party
4 Pizzas: $42.00


Step 2 (2 pts). Calculate and output the sales tax (7%). Calculate and output the delivery charge (20% of cost including tax). Submit for grading to confirm 2 tests pass.
Ex: If the input is:

10  2.6  10.50

The output is:

Friday Night Party
4 Pizzas: $42.00
Tax: $2.94
Delivery: $8.99


Step 3 (2 pts). Calculate and output the total including pizza, tax and delivery. Submit for grading to confirm 3 tests pass.
Ex: If the input is:

10  2.6  10.50

The output is:

Friday Night Party
4 Pizzas: $42.00
Tax: $2.94
Delivery: $8.99
Total: $53.93


Step 4 (2 pts). Repeat steps 1 - 3 with additional inputs for Saturday night (one order per line). Maintain and output a separate total for both parties. Submit for grading to confirm 5 tests pass.
Ex: If the input is:

9   2.5   10.95
14   3.2   14.95

The output is:

Friday Night Party
3 Pizzas: $32.85
Tax: $2.30
Delivery: $7.03
Total: $42.18

Saturday Night Party
6 Pizzas: $89.70
Tax: $6.28
Delivery: $19.20
Total: $115.17

Weekend Total: $157.35


Step 5 (2 pts). Repeat steps 1 - 3 with additional inputs for Sunday night (one order per line). Maintain and output a total for all parties. Submit for grading to confirm all tests pass.
Ex: If the input is:

6   2.8   10.95
22   2.1   12.95
12   1.8   14.95

The output is:

Friday Night Party
3 Pizzas: $32.85
Tax: $2.30
Delivery: $7.03
Total: $42.18

Saturday Night Party
6 Pizzas: $77.70
Tax: $5.44
Delivery: $16.63
Total: $99.77

Sunday Night Party
3 Pizzas: $44.85
Tax: $3.14
Delivery: $9.60
Total: $57.59

Weekend Total: $199.53

I would like for you to make a video where you discuss your project and cover the material from your document. The video is worth 50 points.

Many thanks to Tiffany Thiessen and her team for creating this template.

 

Additional notes from the syllabus:

Project 1

 

The big push this project is for you to really think through what you are going to do this semester to add something to your resume. If you can get it done in a single page, cool. If it takes you 50 pages, I understand. There is no example length. The good students that are really working on something cool usually have more than 2 pages, because they have lots of cool links that they want to work through that will help them with their project. The uninteresting projects can be done in less than a page.

This week you are making the plan. You are giving the things you will work through and spelling out when you will work through them. You are explaining why this matters to you. I would suggest you try to articulate why it matters to an employer as well.

For picking a project, there are no bad answers. If you do something you love, I would tell you to keep doing that. If you do something you hate, now you know to never do it again. If you pick something related to programming, you will have many friends in the class. If you do something outside of programming, you might have to look farther to find someone to work with you.

I left the requirements broad. This means that about anything you turn in I can count for full credit. The goal is to give you the freedom to choose something that will benefit you and your career. Unfortunately, in order to be able to accept a broad range of styles and career goals from all students, it is difficult to pin down what needs to be done. In the past, I have looked for reasons to give people full credit. I have accepted less than stellar work because they showed effort. This assignment is a pass fail grade, and I pass most anything. This assignment was never about a grade. Unfortunately, the grade is the only way I can get people to make sure they make time to do it. The push behind this is to help you do well on something you believe will benefit you.

The other thing that makes this a hard assignment is that not everyone has given thought to what their career should look like. It is hard to start to develop a skill set to support a career that does not exist.

I am sorry this is challenging. My goal is to help you become familiar with the big challenges of life, such as thinking about your future and owning the preparation process for it. It is my hope that as you become more familiar with these questions, you will be less stressed by them when the test of life comes your way.

Good luck friend. What you do with that freedom is up to you. I hope this helps.

assignments.description:
Hello Friends,

For my finals, I ask you to answer a few reflection questions. I am asking you to do five. You are welcome to answer as many as you need, and to share other reflections if you like. But I would like to see you pick 5 and go from there. Here is a link to the questions. I will also paste them in down below.

https://docs.google.com/document/d/1m3XZ5IFSUxRBs_P2B1-Q-qwn2i3ioebpTxWNcDMBAAs/edit?usp=sharing (Links to an external site.)

I ask that you pick your favorite 5 questions to answer. These are pass/fail, so any answer is acceptable. Feel free to take as much time as you need, and use any resources you like.

I also ask that you share a favorite meme or quote or something that stands out to you personally.

If we have a scheduled time to meet for a final, I will be in the room at that time, and you are welcome to join me, but you are not required to make an appearance. An online file submission is fine.

Thank you for all your hard work this semester.

Respectfully,

Jeremy

 

 

The final will be graded pass fail. You get full credit for any answer you give, as long as you give an answer. You may get bonus points for great answers. These are open book, open note, open internet, call a friend or family member questions. Take as much time as you like, and feel free to resubmit if you change your mind later.

Pick your favorite five questions to answer (5 or more)

And if you have a question you would rather talk about, please tell me what that question is and then answer that question.

and

please share your most relatable meme after completing this semester.

 

  1. How were you able to help others during the semester?
  2. What can I do as a faculty, through the syllabus, as well as my own behavior, to encourage the types of behavior you want to see in yourself to make you a better classmate?
  3. Explain the greatest opportunity you took advantage of this semester.
  4. What steps did you take this semester towards your career this semester and explain why it was important to you.
  5. Describe the area that you showed the most personal growth in during this class and explain what helped you make that improvement.
  6. Explain what your favorite assignment was and why it was your favorite.
  7. If you could award a prize to a classmate or someone outside of class, what would it be and why?
  8. Describe your best tools for getting the support you needed for this class.
  9. What was your favorite non-school activity from this semester?
  10. Describe the biggest obstacle you have overcome this semester and explain what kept you moving forward.
  11. What was your favorite part of the semester and what made it stand out?
  12. What has been a positive change that happened during the pandemic and how has this helped you?
  13. Describe your plan for getting to know about job opportunities and expectations for companies you would like to work for.
  14. Describe your best degree related experience this semester.
  15. If you could award a prize to yourself, what would it be and why?
  16. Share three resume bullets you added this semester.
  17. Describe three certifications you would like to earn, when you will get them, and why they are important to you.
  18. What parts of this semester, year, or college experience do you think will stay with you the longest and why?
  19. What are some of the most interesting discoveries you have made this semester, and why are they important to you?
  20. What were some of your most meaningful milestones this semester and why did they matter so much to you?

Project 1

 

The big push this project is for you to really think through what you are going to do this semester to add something to your resume. If you can get it done in a single page, cool. If it takes you 50 pages, I understand. There is no example length. The good students that are really working on something cool usually have more than 2 pages, because they have lots of cool links that they want to work through that will help them with their project. The uninteresting projects can be done in less than a page.

This week you are making the plan. You are giving the things you will work through and spelling out when you will work through them. You are explaining why this matters to you. I would suggest you try to articulate why it matters to an employer as well.

For picking a project, there are no bad answers. If you do something you love, I would tell you to keep doing that. If you do something you hate, now you know to never do it again. If you pick something related to programming, you will have many friends in the class. If you do something outside of programming, you might have to look farther to find someone to work with you.

I left the requirements broad. This means that about anything you turn in I can count for full credit. The goal is to give you the freedom to choose something that will benefit you and your career. Unfortunately, in order to be able to accept a broad range of styles and career goals from all students, it is difficult to pin down what needs to be done. I am sorry this is challenging. My goal is to help you become familiar with the big challenges of life, such as thinking about your future and owning the preparation process for it. It is my hope that as you become more familiar with these questions, you will be less stressed by them when the test of life comes your way.

Good luck friend. What you do with that freedom is up to you. I hope this helps.

Grading Structure:

Use Object Oriented Code in your Choose Your Own Adventure Game

50 bonus points for a fun story.

200 bonus points for the most fun story

200 bonus points for best overall game

Everyone gets 75 bonus points if no one has anything terribly offensive by 

If you do not present in class, you will need to submit a document presenting your work in the discussion, including your code, the results from your code running, and any additional information.



  • 25 points: Demonstration of effort, but no working codes
  • 100 points: Have solution working
  • Bonus:
    • 10 points: All three programming solutions working with some improvement on one problem.
    • 20 points: All three programming solutions working with some improvement on two problems.
    • 30 points: All three programming solutions working with some improvement on three problems.
    • 25 points: You record a video and talk about how or why you worked one of your problems the way you did
    • 25 points: Anyone that presents during class.

There are several ways to make a media based discussion. One option is to use the media button on Canvas Discussions. This lets you record only audio or audio and video. I have not figured out how to share a screen and narrate it yet.

A second option is to use a web based tool such as https://screencast-o-matic.com/ This is nice because it is free and it provides you with a link you can easily share to the discussion. And you can interact with your screen while you are using it.

A third option is to use a service like Zoom to record the video (free) and then post the video on YouTube (also free) The downside is that YouTube wants you to set up an account usually and you have to install Zoom on your computer.

A fourth option, is to use Google Drive or Drobox to store videos and use their servers to share a link. Please let me know if you need any help getting things going.

 

Programming Assignment

Demonstrate your ability to program and do something fun.
